content:
Ben (support): seeing a customer escalation — lots of 502s and timeouts for hosted inference in us-central4 starting ~03:10 UTC. multiple customers reporting auth retries and failed requests. logs show upstream 502s from gateway.
Alice (sre): confirmed, alerting dashboard shows gateway 502 spike + increased SYN retransmits to model backends. request latencies jump before 502s.
Carla (cs): customer says requests succeed on retry but causes user-visible failures, urgent for two enterprise customers.
Ben (support): quick paste of error snippet: `upstream returned 502 while reading response header from upstream` repeated. stack traces point to TLS handshake resets.
Devon (network): pulling pcap now from edge node eu-west4 -> us-central4 path. initial suspicion: PMTU/fragmentation causing TLS records to be dropped (we've seen this with some transit vendors).
ops-oncall-bot: started capture job capture-id=cap-1755-us-central4-03:20 (pcap stored in /mnt/pcaps).
Ben (support): any repro steps we can give customers? they can reproduce reliably from a few subnets.
Alice (sre): repro steps we used: run from customer subnet -> curl -v https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' repeated 3x. first attempt often times out/502, second attempt succeeds.
Devon (network): ran traceroute and MTU probe:
```
traceroute -F -n -w 1 -q 1 api.redwood.example
traceroute to api.redwood.example (35.201.12.34), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.1.2.1  0.6 ms
 2  203.0.113.2  2.1 ms
 3  198.51.100.45  12.3 ms
 4  198.51.100.82  *
```
and `tracepath -n api.redwood.example` returned a MTU drop between our edge and provider hop (reported MTU 1400).
Devon (network): tcpdump shows lots of `IP reassembled` warnings and duplicate ACKs, plus TLS records cut off mid-record. corroborates PMTU blackhole.
Alice (sre): logs from the gateway show repeated `tlsv1 alert unknown ca`? actually it's just incomplete TLS record; upstream closed.
Ben (support): so the hypothesis: some provider hop is silently dropping ICMP too-big leading to fragmentation not working, big TLS records get dropped -> handshake/bulk response fails -> gateway returns 502.
Devon (network): recommended immediate mitigations: 1) enable TCP MTU probing on affected edge hosts: `sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1` 2) apply MSS clamp on iptables for egress to clamp to 1360: `iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu` 3) fail traffic to secondary transit/peer for the prefix.
Alice (sre): I'm going to toggle tcp_mtu_probing on the gateway fleet in us-central4 now (rolling 10% -> 50% -> 100%). will monitor 502 rate.
infra-bot: patch rollout started: tcp_mtu_probing=true rollout_id=rl-622 (10% nodes).
Carla (cs): pinging the customers with repro steps and timeline and that we're rolling mitigations. they asked for ETA for full fix.
Devon (network): opened ticket with provider (ASN 64512 / peer-id 20345). included pcap + tracepath output + example time windows. provider asked for sample PCAP + tcpdump from us-central4 edge and customer IP. ticket ref: PROVIDER-8921.
Ben (support): customer asked if there is an interim app-level workaround. any suggestions?
Alice (sre): best short-term is retries with exponential backoff (they're already seeing second attempt succeed). also reduce TLS record size by enabling smaller write buffer on client if application can control it (lower max payload per request).
Devon (network): provider responded: they see PMTU change to 1400 on one of their transit hops; their firewall drops ICMP. next step from them: either enable ICMP allowed for PMTU or we (Redwood) clamp MSS on our edge / or reroute via alternate peer. they pushed a config change to allow ICMP on their firewall (staged).
ops-oncall-bot: monitoring rule: if gateway 502 rate > 3% for 5m escalate to SEV2.
Alice (sre): after enabling tcp_mtu_probing on 50% nodes we see 502s drop 60% within 6 minutes. starting MSS clamp rollout to egress chains now.
Devon (network): applying iptables clamp on us-central4-egress-1: `iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --set-mss 1360` then save. doing dry-run on 2 nodes.
Carla (cs): customers acknowledged mitigation, one wants an RCA and permanent fix.
Alice (sre): permanent fix options: 1) keep MSS clamp on egress for affected peers 2) operator with provider to fix firewall to allow ICMP too-big 3) prefer routing via alternate peer/backup transit for those prefixes. we'll draft RCA after provider confirms fix.
Ben (support): collecting timeline + affected customer list. I'll coordinate on billing credit asks.
Devon (network): posted provider ticket link and pcap: https://provider-ticketing.example/PROVIDER-8921 (internal). added pcap id cap-1755-us-central4-03:20.
Alice (sre): notes for postmortem: add end-to-end MTU checks to our deployment regression suite; add synthetic tests that send large TLS records to detect PMTU blackholes early.
ops-oncall-bot: update: rollout complete 100% tcp_mtu_probing + MSS clamp applied on us-central4 (18 nodes). 502s back to baseline.
Carla (cs): told customers fix applied, will follow up with RCA and provider ticket.
Ben (support): closing loop once provider confirms permanent firewall change or we keep clamp as long-term. thanks team. :thumbsup:
